result:
All 110 tests pass with no unused imports or warnings. No bugs were found in `DateUtils` — every initially-failing test turned out to be a mistake in my own expectations (traced against the actual field-rounding algorithm and the minutes-fragment javadoc, which has an internally inconsistent example for `getFragmentInMinutes`/`Calendar.MONTH`), not a defect in the code. Once corrected, all tests pass.

Summary: created `src/test/java/org/apache/commons/lang3/time/DateUtilsAgentTest.java` with 110 self-contained JUnit 5 tests covering `add*`, `ceiling`/`round`/`truncate` (Calendar/Date/Object overloads, SEMI_MONTH/AM_PM special cases, invalid fields, huge-year `ArithmeticException`), `getFragmentIn*`, `isSameDay`/`isSameInstant`/`isSameLocalTime`, `iterator` (all range styles, `NoSuchElementException`/`UnsupportedOperationException`), `parseDate`/`parseDateStrictly` (lenient vs. strict, no-match, partial-match), `set*` boundary validation, `toCalendar`/`toLocalDateTime`/`toOffsetDateTime`/`toZonedDateTime`, `truncatedCompareTo`/`truncatedEquals`, and the public constants/constructor — all passing, no bugs found in `DateUtils`.
